t: LeetCode 3238 – Find the Number of Winning Players
o: Player i wins if some color appears among their picks more than i times (strictly more than i balls of one color). With n ≤ 10 and at most 100 picks, simply tally counts[player][color] and check each player. In example 1, player 1 has two color-0 balls (needs ≥ 2 → wins) while player 2's best is two of one color (needs ≥ 3 → loses).
k: A single 2D tally of (player, color) answers everything.
Win condition: any color count for player i exceeds i.

a.i: Accumulate counts in a small 2D array while reading pick, then for each player scan the ≤ 11 colors and test count > i.
s: For each [x, y] in pick, cnt[x][y]++.
Answer = number of players i with max_y cnt[i][y] > i.
a.t: O(P + n·C) with P ≤ 100 picks and C = 11 colors — effectively constant

a.i: Equivalent formulation using a Counter per player instead of a dense 2D array — handy when the color range were large.
s: Map each player to a Counter of colors.
For each player, win if any counter value exceeds the player index.
a.t: O(P + n·distinct colors) — tiny under the constraints

w: Trivial problem — the only traps are off-by-one in the threshold (strictly more than i, i.e., ≥ i+1) and remembering player 0 wins with any ball. Follow-up: report WHICH players win, or handle huge n with sparse counting (same hash-map approach).
